panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Shows the impacted bolus at the site of the ring, part of the clinical presentation of Schatzki ring obstruction. B: Definitively shows a circular mucosal ring in the esophagus, characteristic of Schatzki ring, as noted in the caption. C: Shows mucosal findings related to the recent removal of the bolus and impaction, which is associated with Schatzki ring. D: Provides clear visualization of the mucosal ring confirming the diagnosis of Schatzki Ring.

panels.figure_caption: Endoscopic findings of impacted food bolus and distal esophageal ring. Panels A-D show the impacted food bolus, post-disimpaction mucosal erythema, and the distal esophageal ring identified after bolus removal, consistent with Schatzki ring.
in_text_mentions: ered, suggesting partial luminal obstruction. A 3-cm hiatal hernia was also noted. Mild gastritis was seen and biopsied. The duodenal bulb and second portion of the duodenum appeared normal. Esophageal biopsies were deferred during the index procedure because the EGD was performed urgently to relieve the impacted food bolus, and additional mucosal manipulation was avoided in the setting of acute impaction with local edema and mucosal trauma. An outpatient repeat EGD with esophageal biopsies was recommended to evaluate for eosinophilic esophagitis. The endoscopic findings are shown in Figure 1.
